fallback.text: A PID controller drives a lightly damped plant (natural frequency 4 rad/s, damping 0.4, 50 ms dead time) to a step of the setpoint from 0 to 1 at t = 0.5 s. A proportional controller alone (Kp = 1) overshoots by about 50 % and settles at 0.5, far from the setpoint. With Kp = 2, Ki = 3 and Kd = 0.4 the integral removes the steady-state error and the derivative damps the oscillation: no overshoot, settled within 2 % in about 1.5 s.
